page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute workloads. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1770.0 and a multi-core score of 6838.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only cached small block speed of 530.44 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write performance drops to 37.65 GB/sec, aligning with its weak PassMark memory score. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% at 36.22 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates solid capabilities in specialized tasks, processing 9.71 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining a static web serving throughput of 12.95 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a medium 7B model is limited, with text generation speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 6.31 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for mainstream business applications without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of Intel AMX allows it to handle light AI inference workloads, such as prompt processing, more efficiently than standard legacy processors. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate Redis caching layers.
